blocks.0x00000000:
Trap table 0 (%tbr = 0x0000, used by MID 8). Four copies of the table
live at 0x0000/0x1000/0x2000/0x3000: POST sets %tbr = (MID-8) << 12
(post_slave_idle_loop 0x4758, mp_slave_setup_mmu 0x1ec64) so each CPU has its
own table (and get_mid_from_tbr 0xe794 can recover the MID). The copies are
identical except tt 0: here the reset vector `ba reset_entry`, in copies 1-3
`ba post_entry` (0x4000). Every other vector is
`sethi/or %l4 = handler; jmp %l4; rd %psr, %l0`.
blocks.0x00001000:
Trap table 1 (%tbr = 0x1000, MID 9); identical to table 0 except
tt 0 = `ba post_entry`. The reset path enters POST through this vector:
reset_jump_post 0x26174 jumps to 0xf0001000 (the boot-mode alias of 0x1000).
blocks.0x00002000: Trap table 2 (%tbr = 0x2000, MID 10); copy of table 1.
blocks.0x00003000: Trap table 3 (%tbr = 0x3000, MID 11); copy of table 1.
blocks.0x00004000:
post_entry - POST start, reached from trap table 1..3 tt 0 (boot-mode fetch
0xf0004000) on every CPU. Arbiter enable = 0xf (all CPUs), %tbr = 0,
%wim = 0, %psr = 0xe0, then jump to the low VA alias 0x403c.

get_module_type; the `ba` at 0x4048 makes the SuperSPARC-II BIST check
at 0x4050 dead code. MID != 8 -> post_slave_idle_loop. The master waits
0x20000 loops, sets the interrupt target (pa 0xf_f141_0010) = 0,
%psr = 0x10e0 (EF, S, PS, ET), %tbr = 0, %wim = 0 and initialises ttya/ttyb
(post_zs_init_serial).

blocks.0x000040fc:
post_iu_globals_test (runs before any RAM is used, no name string): write 0 to
%g1-%g7 and test each for 0, then write -1 and compare each with %g1. Any
mismatch -> post_iu_fail_globals "IU Register File Bit Failure" + dump.
blocks.0x000041dc:
post_iu_window_test: %o0..%o7 = 0..7, then 7 times: `save`, check that
%i0..%i7 = 0..7 (window overlap / CWP decrement; else "IU Register File
Window Pointer"), clear and check ins, write/check -1 in ins, locals, outs
(else "IU Register File Bit Failure" with an In/Local/Out dump), reload
%o0..%o7 = 0..7. %g7 = CWP after the first save (7 with 8 windows) is the
loop count; WIM = 0 so no window traps.
blocks.0x000045a0:
After the IU tests: %psr = 0x10e0, %tbr = 0, %wim = 2. HyperSPARC: reset
reg WD bit -> trap_unexpected_watchdog, MCNTL = (MCNTL & 0x7fff) | 0x40000,
CTPR/CTX/regs 0x1000-0x1200 = 0. Viking: SFSR bit 17 -> watchdog report;
flush the whole TLB (ASI 3 va 0x400), flash-clear I/D caches, CTX = 1,
CTPR = 0x40000 (context table at pa 0x400000). -> post_master_start.
blocks.0x00004698:
post_slave_idle_loop - where every CPU with MID != 8 waits during POST.
mpcntl(6, mid, 3) writes 3 ("idle") into its NVRAM command word, then the
CPU clears its own bit (1 << (MID & 3)) in the arbiter enable register:
it stops on its next MBus access until the master re-enables it. It then
polls mpcntl(7) until the command word has bits 1:0 == 0 (a function
address), waits 1000 loops, reads the address again, sets %tbr =
(MID & 3) << 12, fetches 4 arguments with mpcntl(0xc..0xf), enables traps
(PIL 0) and calls the function; afterwards PIL 15, ET 0 and back to the top.
blocks.0x000047d0:
trap_expected_skip - generic handler (tt 2-4, 0x0a-0x10, 0x20-0x7f,
0x82-0xff). If tt (%tbr[11:4]) == %g5 the trap was expected: clear %g5,
restore %psr and resume after the trapping instruction (jmp %l2; rett
%l2+4). Otherwise trap_unexpected_sync. The same pattern (with small
variations) is used by the tt 1, 7 and 9 handlers.

blocks.0x000048ac:
trap_window_underflow: rotate %wim left, reload the window from [%sp]
through ASI 0x20, retry the restore.
blocks.0x00004954:
tt 9 data_access_exception: expected in %g5 -> skip the instruction. With

blocks.0x000049c0:
Interrupt handlers irq_level_1..15 (tt 0x11..0x1f): the expected level is in
%g5 (or %g6 for a second one); a mismatch -> trap_unexpected_async. %i5 =
(MID & 3) << 12. Soft interrupts are acknowledged by writing bit (16+level)
to this CPU's clear-pending register pa 0xf_f140_n004 and reading
0xf_f140_n000 back; %g7 selects extra device acknowledges (parallel port
level 3/4, DMA2 level 4/6, counters level 10/14, EMC level 15 ...). Return
with jmp %l1; rett %l2 (re-execute the interrupted instruction).
